messages:
Casey: Hey team — a customer opened a support ticket: after they added a few-shot block in their system prompt the tool/function calls started returning malformed args and sometimes plain text instead of JSON. Also seeing higher latency (~1.1s -> 1.8s). Can someone triage?

Miguel: Can you paste the exact payload + a curl repro?

Casey: Here — curl (redacted keys):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call-tool \\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \\
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
  -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-1","messages":[
    {"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant. Examples:\nExample 1:\nUser: charge 5 dollars to card\nTool: charge(amount:\"five\",currency:\"USD\")\nExample 2:\nUser: charge $5\nTool: charge(amount:5,currency:\"USD\")\n"},
    {"role":"user","content":"charge 3 dollars to card"}
  ], "tool":"charge","function_call":"auto"}'
```

Casey: Customer says responses sometimes come back with 200 and body `ok` (plain text) or 400 schema_error: "invalid args". They reproduced by toggling the few-shot examples.

Sara: Sounds like prompt-led schema drift — the first example has amount as a quoted word ("five") which trains the model to emit strings for amount. The model may choose to emit plain text instead of calling the tool if examples mix text and structured calls. Did they include tool docs in the system prompt too?

Casey: Yes, they included tool docs verbatim under system. It's kind of messy.

Miguel: Two quick things to try: 1) remove the few-shot examples or normalize them so types match (+ numeric amounts). 2) set `function_call` explicitly to the tool name to force structured output, e.g., \"function_call\": {\"name\":\"charge\"}. Can you repro with/without examples?

Eli: From our side, I pulled the validator logs for that customer request id and see repeated entries: `schema_validator: arg amount type mismatch: got string 'five' expected number`. Also saw `tool_dispatch: fallback_to_text_output=true` a few times — that line means the router treated the response as non-callable.

Casey: Good catch. Customer examples are literally teaching the model to use strings and free text. That would explain both malformed args and the occasional plain-text `ok`.

Miguel: Short-term mitigation options: server-side coercion for obvious cases (\"five\" -> 5) + stricter validation error messages to customers. Medium-term: detect contradictory few-shots in system prompt and warn at request time (DX improvement). Also a model-side policy: prefer function_call when schema-heavy examples present.

Casey: I'll propose a canary: add a validation-coerce step and a warning header back to the customer when conflicts detected. If that checks out, canary 10% and monitor error rate.

deploy-bot: Scheduling canary: validation-coerce v1 -> 10% in prod in 15m :rocket:

Miguel: I'll try to reproduce locally using their prompt + our validator and post logs. Please include the customer request id when you have it.

Casey: Request id: cus_rq_8b3f2a. Adding the ticket link in thread. Thanks — will follow up with reproduction notes and whether the canary reduced plaintext responses.
